title: Makhuwa language - Wikipedia
text: Makhuwa (Emakhuwa; also spelled Makua and Macua) or Mozambican is the primary Bantu language of northern Mozambique. It is spoken by roughly 5.8 million Makua people, [3] who live north of the Zambezi River, particularly in Nampula Province, which is virtually entirely ethnically Makua. [4]

text: Makhuwa-Marrevone is a stable indigenous language of Mozambique. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
